newsitem.title: USA: Ohio corn, soybean ratings show little change.
newsitem.headline: Ohio corn, soybean ratings show little change.

text.p: Corn and soybean crop ratings changed only slightly after a week of below normal temperatures during the week ended July 13, according to the weekly crop update from the Ohio Agricultural Statistics Service.
Corn was rated 66 percent good to excellent, the same as last week. That rating compared to 38 percent last year.
Soybeans were rated steady with last week at 60 percent good to excellent. That figure was up from 34 a year ago. Blooming was up to 35 percent of acreage from 10 last week and six a year ago.

Winter wheat ratings improved slightly to 64 percent good to excellent from 62 last week and compared to 30 percent at that level a year earlier. Wheat was ripe on 34 percent of acreage, compared to 10 percent last week, the agency said.
Soil moisture ratings fell, with topsoils rated 15 percent surplus versus 24 last week and 73 percent adequate versus 73 last week.
